lines.text: There's a lot of us under one roof. Somebody's always cooking and somebody's always complaining about it.
My family's small, but loud. We argue over the last pickle every single night.
My grandparents still live with us. I hear the same three stories every week, and I'd miss them if they stopped.
That's enough of my family for one day. They'd be embarrassed I said so much.
I've told you all about the household already. Nothing's changed since lunch.
My family? That's a bit close to home, {player}. We've only just met.
I don't talk about my people with someone I barely know.
We eat together every night, all of us, even when someone's sulking. Especially then.
My parents taught me to ask why. They regret it at least once a day.
I've a little cousin who copies everything I do. So I walk backwards everywhere now, just to see.
My family has never left the Leaf. Not once in three generations. I'll be the first.
I keep the family calendar. Birthdays, anniversaries, the day the roof needs checking. Nobody else would.
I look after my parents now. It's no burden. They looked after me for long enough.
There's a few of us. We get on. Quietly.
My grandmother tells stories about a fox who lives in the well. I still check the well.
Everyone in my house works. Even the youngest sorts the beans. That's how we get by.
I've been piecing together our family tree. There's a whole branch nobody will tell me about. Probably dull.
I'd do anything for my family. Anything. I check the locks twice before bed.
My little sister is learning to read. I sit with her every evening. She's so proud of every word.
My family's name is older than the street it lives on. I carry it carefully.
My family's the BEST! Loud, stubborn and the strongest grip on this side of the village!
They're kind to me. They don't push. I'm grateful for that.
My parents served. Their parents served. I serve. It's what we do.
Thank you for telling me, {player}. I won't carry it anywhere it shouldn't go.
That's a lot to hold on your own. You don't have to, you know.
I'm glad you trust me with that. Come and talk any time it gets heavy.
I'm still thinking about what you told me earlier. I'm here if there's more.
We've talked a lot today. Let it settle, {player}. I'm not going anywhere.
I'm glad you'd share, but maybe wait until you know me better.
That sounds important. Keep it a while longer, until you're sure of me.
Oh, come here. You've been carrying that all alone? Not anymore. Eat something, and keep talking.
I'll think about what you said. Carefully. It deserves that.
No jokes. Not for this. Thank you for telling me, {player}. Really.
Everyone's walking some road. Yours sounds harder than most. I'd like to walk some of it with you.
I'll remember every word. Not to hold it against you. To understand you properly.
Then I'll be someone you can count on. Whatever comes. That's a promise.
I... don't really know what to say. I'm not good with this sort of thing.
Thank you. Your story's still being written, you know. The best chapters might be the next ones.
That's hard. And you're still standing. That tells me more about you than any of it.
I've wondered about you for so long, and I'm glad I didn't have to ask. Thank you.
Nobody's going to make you feel that way again. Not while I'm around.
Thank you for trusting me. Take your time. I'll listen to all of it.
You've no reason to be ashamed of any of that. Hold your head up. I will, for you.
That's so unfair! You don't deserve any of it! I'm on your side, {player}, always!
I... I know a little what that's like. Thank you for telling me. Really.
That took courage. More than most missions. I'm proud of you for saying it.
Oh, very funny. I'll get you back for that, {player}.
Ha! Fine, I walked into that one.
You're lucky I like you.
Once was funny. Twice is pushing it.
Running out of material, are we?
We don't know each other well enough for that.
Careful. Teasing's for friends, and we're not there yet.
Cheeky! See if I save you the crispy bit of the rice now.
Hm. That was actually quite clever. I'll laugh later, when I've thought of a reply.
Oh, it's ON. You'd better sleep with one eye open, {player}.
Ha! Says the one who got lost in the bamboo by the river. Twice.
That's not accurate, but it is funny. I'll allow it.
Fair. I deserved that one. Next one's mine, though.
...Hm. Not bad.
You've just given me an idea for a very unflattering painting of you. Thank you.
Funny. Charge you a ryo for every joke at my expense and I'd be rich.
Wait, is that true? Do I really do that? I do, don't I. Oh no.
Laugh all you like. I'll still walk you home.
That's a little mean. ...A little funny, too.
I beg your pardon? Do you know who you're talking to?
WHAT?! Take that back! ...Okay, it was funny. TAKE IT BACK ANYWAY!
Oh... I didn't... is that what people think of me?
That's enough. Mockery is a poor habit, {player}.
I try to leave every place a little better than I found it. That's all.
Keep your word. If you can't keep it, don't give it.
Treat people the same whether they can do something for you or not.
I've preached enough for one day, {player}.
You know what I believe now. Let's see if I live up to it.
What I believe in? That's not something I share with just anyone.
Ask me that when you've seen how I live. Then you'll know.
Kindness and family. Feed people, look after your own, and count everyone as your own.
Know things, and tell the truth about what you know. Everything else follows.
Be free and be kind. Life's too short to be cruel or cooped up.
Courage, and freedom to use it. A wall's only there to be looked over.
Do your duty, and do it well enough that nobody has to check.
Duty and loyalty. Stand where you said you'd stand, with who you said you'd stand by.
Honesty. And being left to live my own way.
Make things. Make the world stranger and more beautiful. And let others do the same.
Tell the truth, pay your debts, do the work. Simple, not easy.
Never stop asking questions. And never let anyone tell you that you can't.
Loyalty to the people you love. Family first, and family is whoever you'd bleed for.
Be kind. Especially to the small things that can't thank you.
Strength, and the honour of my family. One protects the other.
Courage! Loyalty! Never give up on your friends, and never run away!
I think... making something gentle and true is a brave thing. And being kind is, too.
Duty. Loyalty. Discipline holds them together.
Sleep on it. Most things look smaller after breakfast.
Ask the person it concerns, not everyone around them.
When in doubt, do the kind thing and the honest thing. Usually they're the same.
I've given you all my wisdom for today. It's not a deep well, {player}.
Try the advice I gave you first, then come back.
I'm hardly the one to ask. We barely know each other.
Advice from a near stranger? Ask someone who knows you.
Eat first. Then decide. Nobody ever made a good choice hungry.
Write both choices down and read them aloud. You'll hear which one you already want.
Flip a coin. If you're disappointed with how it lands, do the other thing.
Take the road that scares you a little. Not a lot. A little.
Break it into steps. Small ones. Then do the first one today.
Keep the promise you already made. Then worry about the next one.
Say less. Watch more.
Imagine you're telling the story of it years from now. Which version would you be proud of?
What does it cost, and what's it worth? If you can't answer both, you're not ready.
Find out more first. Most bad choices are just choices made too early.
Whatever you do, don't do it alone. Take someone you trust.
Be gentle with yourself. And with whoever's on the other side of it.
Do nothing you'd be ashamed to put your name to. That's my family's rule. Use it.
Go for it! Full force! If it goes wrong, go for it again!
Um. I'd... I'd do the thing that feels a bit brave. Small brave. That's usually right.
Stop asking and start doing. You already know the answer.
I've a dream I've never said out loud. I'll say it to you. Just this once.
Everyone laughs when you're young and say what you want to be. I stopped saying it. I never stopped wanting it.
Some mornings I wake up and the dream feels close enough to touch. Other mornings it's over the mountains.
I've said enough about my dream for one day. Let me keep a little of it to myself.
You've heard it now. Hold me to it, {player}.
My dream? That's... not for someone I barely know.
You haven't earned that one yet, {player}. Not yet.
I want a home full of people, all fed and safe. That's my dream. Is it too small? It feels big to me.
I want to understand one thing completely before I die. I haven't chosen which yet.
Promise you won't laugh. ...You can laugh a little. I mean it, though. Every word.
I want to stand somewhere nobody from the Leaf has ever stood. Then come home and tell you about it.
I have a plan for my dream. Forty steps. I'm on step nine.
It's not a flashy dream. But I'll get there a day at a time. I always do.
I've never told anyone. ...Don't make me regret it.
When I close my eyes I can see it already, every colour. I just have to make the world catch up.
A dream's just a plan nobody's paid for yet. I'm saving up.
I keep wondering whether my dream will look the way I picture it when I get there. Do you think it will?
My dream's about the people I love. Keeping them safe is part of it. All of it, maybe.
It's a quiet dream. I hope that's all right. I think quiet dreams count too.
My dream is worthy of my name. I'll reach it, or I'll fall trying. There's no third choice.
I'm going to do it! I'm going to do it if it takes a hundred years! You'll see!
I've only ever written it in my diary. Saying it out loud is... scary. Here goes.
A dream without discipline is a wish. Mine has a schedule.
I worry I'm running out of time to become who I meant to be.
Some nights I lie awake wondering if I've chosen the wrong road.
I worry about the people I love more than I let them see.
I've said my worries out loud once today. That's enough to get me to sleep.
Thank you for listening earlier. Let's talk about something lighter.
My worries are my own, {player}.
Let's not dig into that. Not with someone I've only just got to know.
I worry I'm not doing enough for everyone. There's always someone hungry I didn't notice.
I worry that I think so much I never actually act. Then the moment's gone.
I worry people think I'm only a joke. That I'll never be taken seriously when it matters.
What if I never leave? What if I'm old in this same street, wondering what was out there?
I'm afraid of the mistake I didn't catch. The one that hurts somebody.
I worry about letting someone down. Once. When it matters. That's the one I couldn't live with.
That I'll keep everyone at arm's length until there's no one left to reach.
I worry the colours will fade. That one day I'll look at the sky and just see sky.
Money. Always money. One bad season and everything I've built is gone.
I worry there's an answer I'll never find. It keeps me up, honestly.
That I won't be there when someone needs me. That I'll be a step too slow.
I worry the world is too hard for soft things. And I'm one of them.
I worry I'll shame my family. That I'm not as strong as they believe.
I worry I'll give it everything and it still won't be enough. ...Don't tell anyone I said that.
That I'll never be brave enough to say the things I really mean.
That I've been too hard on the people I'm trying to make strong. That they'll only remember the hardness.
We've had some good times already, haven't we? I keep a few of them close.
I was just remembering the last time we went out. That was a good day.
I've been through all our good memories once today. Let's make a new one.
We've reminisced enough, {player}. Let's go and do something worth remembering.
We haven't got many memories yet, you and I. Give it time.
Ask me again after we've been out together a few times.
Nothing new since we last talked. Quiet weeks are underrated.
Still waiting to see how things land. I'll tell you as soon as I know.
I've no news beyond what I told you earlier.
Same as this morning, {player}. Nothing's moved.
Nothing to tell yet. Ask me in a week or two.
It's too early to say how it's going.
Not much to report. The well bucket squeaks again, and nobody's oiled it.
Busy morning, slow afternoon. The usual.
Did you see the sky at dawn? Pink all the way to the Hokage Rock.
Let's leave that for when we know each other better.
That's a conversation for another day, I think.
Ask me again in a while, {player}. Not yet.
Them? One of the best people I know. I'd do anything for them.
I'd walk through the rain to bring them soup. That's how I feel about them.
Don't you say a word against them. They're dear to me.
I like them. Good company, always on time.
They're all right. More than all right, honestly.
We get on well. They make me laugh.
I don't really know them. We nod in the street.
Them? Can't say I've an opinion. Seem decent enough.
We've spoken once or twice. Nothing to tell.
We're not close. Let's leave it at that.
They and I don't see eye to eye. It's nothing dramatic.
I keep my distance. It's better for both of us.
I'd rather not talk about them. Or to them.
Honestly? I can't stand them. Don't tell anyone I said it.
If they're coming, I'm leaving. That's all I'll say.
We've done the weather already, {player}. The sky hasn't changed its mind.
Still the same day, still the same squeaky bucket.
Let's start simpler, shall we?
We hardly know each other. Hello is plenty for now.
Grilled mackerel with a squeeze of citrus. Nothing fancier needed.
I'd eat dango every day if my teeth would let me.
Have you tried the eel by the second bridge? They brush it with sauce three times.
We've talked food already today. Now I'm just hungry.
If we keep talking about food, I'll have to go and buy some.
Food? We've only just met. Ask me when we've shared a meal.
Let's get to know each other a little first.
Miso soup, the way my grandmother made it. I'll make you a bowl. No, I insist.
I like plain rice and pickles. You can taste every grain when nothing's shouting over it.
I can fit six dango in my mouth at once. I'll show you. Okay, five. Okay, maybe don't watch.
A merchant once gave me a pepper from the far south. I cried for an hour. I'd do it again.
Rolled omelette, cut into exactly eight. Uneven pieces taste wrong. I can't explain it.
Rice, fish, soup. Same breakfast for twelve years. It's never let me down.
Cold soba. Quiet place. That's it.
Sweet bean buns taste like a lazy afternoon. Do you know what I mean? Purple and slow.
Whatever's freshest and cheapest at the stalls. The fishmonger marks down at four, by the way.
How do they get the broth at Ichiraku so clear? I've asked. They just wink.
You're eating properly, aren't you? Not just ramen? ...Mostly ramen. I knew it.
I like warm sweet potato in winter. I share the skins with the neighbour's dog.
My family's pickling recipe goes back five generations. Nothing in the market compares.
RAMEN! Extra pork! Extra egg! Extra everything! Is there any other answer?
I like... strawberry mochi. Is that silly? It's soft. It doesn't make a fuss.
Food is fuel. Brown rice, grilled fish, and no sweets before a mission.
I'm working on my footwork. Slow, but it's coming.
Training Ground 3 has the best posts. The bark's worn to the shape of a fist.
Every morning, a lap of the outer wall. Some mornings I even enjoy it.
We've already compared bruises today, {player}.
More training talk? Go and actually train, then come back.
I don't talk technique with people I've just met.
Let's leave training for when we've sparred once or twice.
I mostly train so I can carry the shopping up the hill without stopping. It counts!
Most mistakes in a spar happen in the head first. I train my thinking as much as my arms.
I train by racing the pigeons off the roofs. They win. For now.
I climb the cliff behind the falls. No ropes. Don't tell anyone. Want to come?
Three hundred strikes, logged. Then I check where the misses went and adjust.
Same drills every day. They're dull. That's why they work.
I train alone. Early. Before anyone's watching.
I pretend the training post is a mountain troll. It helps more than you'd think.
Train what you'll use. Fancy jutsu won't help if you can't run for an hour.
Why does a spinning kunai fly straighter? I threw two hundred to find out. Still not sure.
I practise guarding more than striking. Someone has to stand in front.
Oh... I don't really like fighting talk. Could we talk about something else?
I train harder than anyone my age. That's not a boast. Ask the posts.
A thousand kicks before breakfast! Then a thousand more! Want to join? You want to!
I practise throwing at night, when nobody can see me miss. I'm getting better. A little.
Train until the movement is boring. Then train it until it's yours.
Oh, go on. ...No, really, go on, say it again.
That's kind of you, {player}. You made my morning.
You noticed? Nobody notices. Thank you.
Twice in one day? You'll turn my head, {player}.
Careful, you'll use up all your nice words on me.
That's... a bit much from someone I barely know. But thank you.
Flattery already? We've only just met.
Aren't you sweet! Here, have a rice cake for that.
Thank you. I'll think about that, actually. It's nice to be seen.
I KNOW. But it's nice to hear. Say it in a funny voice this time.
Ha! Thanks. Tell that to the mountain that nearly threw me off last week.
You noticed the stitching? Six hours. Thank you. Truly.
Thank you, {player}. That means more from you than most.
...Don't. I don't know what to do with that.
That's the nicest thing I've heard all week. I'm going to paint it. Somehow.
Kind words don't pay the rent. But fine. Thank you. Now, was there something you needed?
Really? What makes you say that? No, I want to know, tell me exactly.
Thank you. Now you look after yourself as well as you say I do.
Oh. That's lovely of you. I'll keep that one somewhere safe.
Naturally. ...But I'm glad it was you who said it.
YES! Thank you! Now I'm fired up for the whole day!
M-me? Oh. Thank you. I don't... thank you.
Hm. Praise is easy. But I'll accept it. Once.
The tea house is putting in a second bench by the river. Big news, for our street.
They're repainting the gate posts. Somebody chose a very loud red.
The bathhouse raised its prices by a ryo. People are furious. Quietly.
That's all the news I've got. I'm not making any up.
You've heard the lot, {player}. Come back tomorrow for fresh gossip.
I don't pass gossip to people I've only just met.
News? Maybe once I know where it'll end up.
The baker's daughter is walking now! Wobbly as a new foal. The whole lane cheered.
The Academy library had a flood in the cellar. They're drying the scrolls on the roof, page by page.
Somebody painted a moustache on the scarecrow by the farms. It wasn't me. It was definitely not me.
A caravan came in from the far east this morning. Silk, spices and a goat with a hat.
The Mission Desk changed its filing order. Nobody can find anything. I've offered to help.
The night watch doubled on the east wall for the season. Nothing wrong, just careful.
I don't keep up with gossip. Ask someone else.
The wisteria by the shrine bloomed overnight. People say it does that when a baby's born on the street.
Rice is up two ryo a sack. Buy now if you can, it'll be worse after the rains.
Did you hear? Someone found a tunnel under the old storehouse. Just a root cellar, probably. Probably!
There's a loose dog near the market biting at ankles. Mind the little ones if you see it.
The kennel had a litter of pups. Seven! They're looking for homes.
Our clan's youngest passed the Academy entrance with the top mark. As expected.
There's going to be a sumo match at the stadium! I'm entering! Probably! Maybe!
The flower shop has a new colour of iris. Sort of a grey-blue. I went to look three times.
Two Genin were caught on the Hokage Rock after curfew. Laps till dawn. Rightly so.
I whittle little animals in the evenings. I've a shelf of crooked foxes.
I keep a garden box on the sill. Two radishes this year. Champion radishes.
I collect river stones. Smooth ones. My shelves are getting heavy.
I've bored you with my hobby enough for one day.
That's my hobby, the whole of it. There's no more to tell today.
What I do with my evenings is my own business. For now.
That's a bit personal for someone I've just met.
I knit. Scarves, hats, little covers for teapots. Everyone on the lane has one whether they want it or not.
I read. Histories mostly. I keep notes in the margins, which the librarian forgives me for.
I make up games. My latest is roof tag, where the ground is lava. Rules are still evolving.
I draw maps. Every path in the woods I've walked. There's a lot of blank paper left.
I keep a bonsai. Eleven years. I trim it with tweezers on the first of every month.
I carve handles for tools. A good handle lasts longer than the blade. I like that.
Calligraphy. Alone. One word, a hundred times, until it's right.
I paint. Mostly the sky, but sometimes the sky as it ought to be. More purple.
I fix broken things and sell them on. Profitable, and it keeps the hands busy.
I take clocks apart. Putting them back together is the part I'm still learning.
I teach the little ones on my street to fall without hurting themselves. Somebody should.
I look after the stray cats by the shrine. They have names. They don't answer to them.
I study my family's records. Every name, every deed. I'll add my own one day.
Training IS my hobby! And eating after training! And then more training!
I fold paper cranes. I'm at four hundred and twelve. I'm not counting for any reason. Well...
I keep my blades. Sharpen, oil, wrap. Every night. A habit of discipline.
Who, the new family by the well? Pleasant enough. They keep chickens.
I try not to say much about people who aren't here to answer.
Everyone's got a story, {player}. I only know the cover of most of them.
We've done enough talking about other people today. Let's give them a rest.
I've said all I'll say about them for now.
Gossip about the neighbours? Not with a near stranger, {player}.
Let's not start on other folk just yet.
Oh, I know everyone! Well, I know something about everyone. Who are we talking about?
I don't discuss people behind their backs. Neither should you.
I only know good things about my neighbours. I make sure of it, I feed them all.
I mind my own. They mind theirs.
I could tell you who snores loudest on this street. But then I'd have to admit how I know.
